sources.outlet: U.S. Department of Labor Office of Inspector General
sources.quote: These mine operators could avoid the financial responsibility for the violation penalties by selling the mine or possibly declaring bankruptcy.
sources.searcher_note: PDF. OIG audit of MSHA civil penalties: mines that changed ownership had worse safety records (46% vs 26% with violations), 'by changing ownership, mine operators could also escape financial responsibility for past violation penalties'; ~30% of mines changed operators 2000-2017; 25% of operators did not pay in full. National, no unpaid-share split by handoff vs closure, no Blackjewel/Brody.

sources.quote: will not inherit the dozens of delinquent fines levied by the federal Mine Safety and Health Administration (MSHA) for safety violations at the Casselman mine
sources.searcher_note: One handoff case: bankrupt Corsa Coal's Casselman mine (Garrett County, MD) goes to Rosebud Mining without its delinquent MSHA fines (just under $25,000). Maryland, not Central Appalachia; no share or comparison.

sources.quote: MSHA says it does not have the legal authority to deny mine operators the ability to open new mines due to unpaid fines.
sources.searcher_note: NPR on the 2019 OIG audit: auditors recommended barring operators with outstanding penalties from new mines; MSHA says it lacks authority.

sources.outlet: NPR (with Mine Safety and Health News)
sources.quote: An NPR investigation found thousands of American mine owners fail to pay penalties for safety violations
sources.searcher_note: Earliest found: NPR/MSHN 'Delinquent Mines' series, nearly $70M in delinquent MSHA penalties; about unpaid fines generally, not handoffs vs closures.

sources.quote: Justice said some of those fines should go to the mine's previous owner and that he shouldn't be required to pay them.
sources.searcher_note: Handoff dispute in Central Appalachia: Justice family re-bought Bluestone from Mechel in 2015 and argues MSHA fines belong to the prior operator. Pattern example; not the lead's operators.

notes: No source found naming Blackjewel/Revelation Energy or Brody Mining with unpaid MSHA civil penalties, and none reporting unpaid-share rates for handoff vs closed mines (16.6% vs 13.0%, or the builder's 28.7% vs 3.7%). The pattern itself - operators shedding MSHA penalty debt by selling or transferring a mine - is stated by the DOL OIG 2019 audit and illustrated by one Maryland case (CNS 2025) and the Justice/Bluestone dispute (WCHS 2019). Checked, not recorded: ProPublica/Mountain State Spotlight 2023-04-26 on Blackjewel bankruptcy (its '$600,000 in unpaid fines' at Foresters mine are Kentucky state environmental fines, not MSHA); WV Gazette-Mail 2024-10-19 on $17.3M total MSHA delinquent debt (Justice and Lexington Coal named, not Blackjewel with a figure); WVPB 2013 Brody Mine story on pattern-of-violations status (no unpaid-fine figure). No coverage dated after 2026-06-30 found. Search stopped at 9 per the coordinator's budget note.
